hypothesis: Iter 79 = ROLLOUT-DEDUP REFACTOR to make the deferred iter-78 honest baseline tractable (measurement-first). CONTEXT: iter 78's joint-aux-step fix was validated in phase 1 (50/50 epochs, no NaN, aux losses converge) but its honest benchmark was DEFERRED — a full run never completed because one phase-2 epoch is ~1.6h (the three heavy signals are sequential Python loops: cohort_statistic ~1754s over 31 specs, physiology_rules ~2100s over 61 rules, cold_distill ~1339s), so 10 phase-2 epochs run ~16h and the dispatched runs timed out before writing a report. This iter makes the two heaviest signals structurally cheaper WITHOUT changing what they compute, so the run completes and emits the real iter-78 numbers. CHANGE 1 (physiology_rules, arm-major): the 61 rules reference only 10 distinct arm protocols, but the iter-68 rule-major loop re-rolled each arm once PER RULE (115 rollouts = 77,880 integration steps/epoch). Inverted to arm-major: roll each distinct (arm.label, init_mode) ONCE and score every rule that uses it against the shared trajectory (10 rollouts = 8,040 steps/epoch — 9.7x less step-work). CHANGE 2 (cohort_statistic, protocol batching): 31 specs collapse to 18 distinct arm protocols (four extended-fast 1440-step specs, four OGTT, four sleep-dip specs each share a protocol, differing only in marker/window/target); group same-protocol specs by their frozen .arms tuple and roll each protocol ONCE over the group's stacked per-spec cold-init states (45,240 -> 28,500 steps/epoch, 1.59x). WHY GRADIENT-IDENTICAL (the whole point — the baseline must be the TRUE iter-78 number): both losses are means over (units x patients) of per-rollout terms, and mean/sum are linear, so each rollout's contribution is a separable partial loss; ONE backward per arm-group / protocol-group accumulates into .grad exactly as one backward per rule/spec did (PyTorch additive-grad — the same linearity the iter-68 per-rule/per-spec memory fix already relies on). Peak memory is <= before (one group's rollout graph live at a time). Guarded by new per-parameter gradient-equivalence tests (test_physiology_rules_signal, test_cohort_signal) asserting the refactored path reproduces the old path's reported loss AND every model+embedding gradient to float-32 tolerance. CONFIG HELD BYTE-IDENTICAL to iter 78 (all 48 trainArgs unchanged) so the benchmark is attributable as the deferred iter-78 baseline, not a confounded new recipe.
expectedEffect: PRIMARY (the bar iter 78 deferred): the run COMPLETES both phases within the 24h Cloud Run task-timeout (phase-2 epoch ~1.6h -> ~0.9h: physiology ~2100->~300s, cohort ~1754->~1100s; ~12h total wall-clock incl. ~2.7h phase-1) and writes benchmark-report.json. With that, the first HONEST iter-78 baseline: (1) per_marker_by_source['real'] skill_vs_persistence for glucose/hr/sbp/dbp/temp (glucose skill is a hard bar — persistence ~0.014 — so near-zero/negative is honest, not a regression); (2) overall_weighted_mape_by_source split real vs teacher; (3) textbook_mean_pass_rate (gate live at 0.45); (4) dist_insulin/dist_lactate/dist_hepatic_output in cold-distill telemetry (iter-77's level anchors, finally exercised in a completed phase 2); (5) aux losses tracking their weights coherently. NO modeling change — the benchmark reflects the iter-78 model exactly (refactors are gradient-identical, test-guaranteed); the only deltas vs a hypothetical un-refactored iter-78 run are float-32 reduction-order rounding (~1e-7). RISKS: (R1) if it still times out, the heavy remainder is cold_model_distillation (~1339s; its inner Adam anchor-calibration is sequential and was deliberately NOT batched here — it needs a riskier integrate() API change); next lever is batching its 8 level-anchor windows or tuning recalib cadence. (R2) cohort grouping batches same-protocol specs into one SxB rollout — peak memory for the largest group (5 specs x 7 embeddings = 35-wide x 1440 steps, checkpointed) is ~5x a single-spec rollout but far below the all-31-specs graph that caused the iter-67 OOM; if it OOMs, lower cohort-sample-patients or cap group size. (R3) grouping key is spec.arms value-equality — near-identical-but-unequal protocols stay separate (correctness preserved, just less speedup).
